1,000 days. This week marked 1,000 days since Israel's genocide of Gaza began.
1,000 days of near-daily bombings. 1,000 days of [forced
displacement](https://zeteo.com/p/gaza-ceasefire-death-toll-1000-israel-
palestinians-genocide), [starvation](https://zeteo.com/p/israel-starvation-
policy-gaza), and a [lack of adequate medical care](https://zeteo.com/p/watch-
now-gaza-doctors-under-attack). 1,000 days of the world largely ignoring a
genocide broadcast live on our screens, of babies with [parts of their skulls
blown off](https://zeteo.com/p/october-7-one-year-genocide-israel-children),
of Israeli soldiers [gleefully showing evidence](https://zeteo.com/p/israel-
soldier-gaza-genocide-instagram-facebook) of their war crimes, of people being
[burned alive](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2025/4/8/palestinians-
mourn-journalist-burned-alive-in-israeli-strike-on-gaza-
tent#flips-6371235254112:0), or
[raped](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qmjGdzyj5BA), or
[tortured](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/videos-israeli-soldiers-abuse-
palestinian-detainees-rcna123214).

The truth is, however, the Nakba, the dehumanization have gone on for much
longer than 1,000 days. And will likely continue for many more, so long as
Israel continues to receive the backing of the U.S. and much of the West.
